$comment: Known failures of the deterministic integration tier on PostgreSQL, each with its root cause. integration.yml (integration-postgres) runs this ratchet on every PR the SQL Server lane runs on, and on the release. It fails on a failure NOT listed here and on a KnownFailures entry that passes, so remove an entry in the pull request that fixes it. Flaky entries depend on runner speed and never fail the job either way; keep that list short and give each a cause. Delete this file, and gate on zero failures, when both lists are empty.

KnownFailures.realtime-deterministic.RD9: Since #6517 (Predictive Studio PR 4): the publish locks run the stored queries 'Predictive Studio: Lock Pipeline For Publish' / '… Lock Model For Publish', which are SQL Server-only (`[__mj]."MLTrainingPipeline" WITH (UPDLOCK, HOLDLOCK, NOWAIT)`); on PostgreSQL they fail with `syntax error at or near "["`, and because PostgreSQL aborts the whole transaction on an error, the next read in it (ML Model OutputSemantics) fails with 'current transaction is aborted'. Needs PostgreSQL variants of the two lock queries (e.g. SELECT … FOR UPDATE NOWAIT). Found by the v6.3.0-edge.2 build.
KnownFailures.realtime-deterministic.RD11: PostgreSQL aborts the whole transaction on an error. The two concurrent accepts share one provider, so the second joins the first's transaction and the loser's unique violation takes the winner down too.
KnownFailures.realtime-deterministic.RD13: PG metadata: MJ: AI Personas.Name is recorded as Length 100 (50 characters) for an NVARCHAR(100) column. SQL Server's R__RefreshMetadata heals Length; the PG R__ deliberately does not.
